title: Verification record for a focused run whose first stage crashed is rejected as "unclassified_stages: no recognized check" instead of recorded as a failed check
outcome: The unclassified refusal for the crashed WinB focused run is explained (an unsupported PowerShell stage argv, refused by design before the outcome is considered), and behavioural tests pin that recognized focused stages record crash-shaped and normal failures as failed and passes as passed, while unsupported commands stay unclassified.
acceptance: The original focused WinB run is diagnosed from the literal planned and observed stage argv and the verifier source. The PowerShell stage ended in a real failure; its unsupported command explains the unclassified native-verification refusal.

A recognized focused test stage that terminates unsuccessfully without a libtest summary is recorded as a failed Test. A recognized normal failure is recorded as failed and a recognized pass as passed. An unsupported focused command remains unclassified for native verification even when it fails.
Behavioral tests use the committed-input verification preparation path to cover the observed wrapper and the recognized crash-shaped, normal-fail and pass cases.
